primary_claim: The empirical spectral distribution of QK circuit correlation matrices in dense (non-MoE) text-to-text transformer models follows consistent trends -- well-fit by a gamma distribution -- that can be used to build a weight-only taxonomy of attention heads without requiring forward passes, with potential to speed up automated circuit discovery and model diffing.

effect.metric: Jensen-Shannon Divergence goodness-of-fit between average ESD and fitted gamma distribution
effect.value: JSD typically in the range 0.0-0.1 across all models studied, indicating a very good fit

contradicts_or_qualifies: Automated Circuit Discovery (Conmy et al. 2023) treats model weights as a passive backdrop for activation-level patching experiments, which makes it difficult to scale; this work proposes using weight structure directly to prune the search space
stated_future_work: Look for functional similarity between ESD-based head classes, e.g. check if low-alpha classes are 'writer' heads (high direct logit attribution) and high-alpha classes are 'aggregator' heads that consolidate information, or vice versa
limitations_stated: Classification B (per-layer ESD statistics) is model-specific, can only group a subset of layers, and lacks a general metric to measure goodness-of-fit
The exact mechanism behind why the mean ESD follows a gamma distribution is not known and is currently only empirical
quote: Empirical Spectral Distribution (ESD) of the correlation matrix of $W_{QK}$ in dense (non-MoE) text-to-text models exhibit certain trends.
